title: Orion Labs - QBR: Usage, Costs, Reliability & Roadmap
summary: Quarterly check-in to review production usage trends, steep cost spikes during promos, reliability incidents in May, and alignment on guardrails and pilot budget commitment for dedicated capacity. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark with a small dedicated pool and share cost model. Security doc and pricing spreadsheet to be sent.
action_items: Maya Patel - Send tailored cost model spreadsheet + example runbook link - due 2026-07-10
Eric Zhao - Share pilot benchmark config (model variant, batch sizes, seq len distribution) and runbook - due 2026-07-09
Sofia Reyes - Confirm target SLAs (p95, throughput) and list of restricted data flows for VPC - due 2026-07-12
Priya Nair - Approve budget band for 30-day dedicated pilot and confirm PO cadence - due 2026-07-14
Janelle Rowe - Schedule kickoff call for pilot and put meeting invite on calendar - due 2026-07-08
next_steps: Redwood to provide 2-week dedicated pilot proposal and cost model
Customer to confirm SSO/SAML and KMS vendors and any enterprise-only compliance docs needed
Run an initial 48 hour burst benchmark during off-peak window and share metrics
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got about an hour. quick roll call?
[00:08] Sofia (Orion): Sofia here, hi.
[00:11] Liam (Orion): Liam on SRE.
[00:13] Priya (Orion): Priya from finance.
[00:15] Eric (Redwood-SE): Eric here, SE.
[00:17] Caleb (Product): Caleb product.
[00:19] Janelle (CSM): Janelle CSM.
[00:21] Unknown Caller: (mumble)
[00:25] Maya: Cool. agenda - usage and cost recap, reliability incidents, go over guardrails and the ask for a pilot/dedicated commit, then next steps. if anything else add.
[01:02] Sofia: Sounds good. Quick context — May had a promo that drove a 4x spike in gen requests and then a few 503s on Friday the 8th. we logged incident with our SREs, but want to understand how Redwood would isolate and prevent noisy-tenant impact.
[01:34] Eric: yeah, we saw the traces in your account — the root cause looked like an autoscaler oscillation + warmup latency on cold KV cache for long sequences. the quick mitigation was circuit breaker to hosted fallback, but for long term we recommend prefix caching plus a small dedicated pool for your peak traffic to avoid noisy neighbor.
[02:01] Liam: can you explain prefix caching again? we heard kv cache earlier but not 100% sure.
[02:08] Eric: sure. prefix or KV cache stores previous token key-values; for repeated multi-turn flows or templated prompts prefix cache can serve large portions from ram instead of recomputing; that reduces p95 quite a bit. in hosted mode, cache is shared and eviction policy can cause misses during spikes. dedicated pool pins capacity and cache warmup is controlled by you. also batching policies matter — continuous batching reduces per-token cost but can add ms latency.
[02:45] Maya: and tradeoff is predictability vs cost. dedicated means pay for reserved capacity but you get predictable tail latency. hosted is cheaper for steady low volume but spikes cause contention.
[03:10] Priya: the bill in May surprised us — avg token cost looked normal but overall spend was 3x our forecast. curious what levers we can pull to reduce peak cost without sacrificing SLA.
[03:30] Eric: two immediate levers: 1) model variant — use a 7B quantized for high throughput for non-critical paths; 2) workload routing — route experimental or lower-confidence traffic to a cheaper model, keep core flows on the higher-quality model. and 3) caching + batching settings. we'll show examples in the cost model.
[04:05] Caleb: are there auto-fallbacks if dedicated pool hits capacity? like we don't want failed requests.
[04:10] Janelle: yes, Redwood supports routing policies with fallback to hosted variants; you can set thresholds and percent rollouts.
[04:16] Sofia: security — we need VPC, KMS integration, and audit logs stored for 3 years. do you have SOC2 plus any ISO certs?
[04:27] Maya: yes SOC2 type II, ISO 27001 in progress, and we have KMS/HSM integrations. i'll send the security pack (redwood security.pdf) and a redacted audit log example. (link: https://redwood.example.com/security.pdf)
[04:44] Liam: for VPC, traffic egress patterns? our compliance team is strict about any external routes.
[04:50] Eric: private deployments keep data plane in your VPC; the control plane is optional private. traffic can be strictly east-west in your network, and we provide network diagrams. we'll annotate the pilot doc.
[05:10] Priya: on pricing cadence — is reserved billed monthly or annually? we need some flexibility for pilot scaling.
[05:18] Maya: reserved is typically monthly commit but we can offer a 30-day pilot with a convertible credit toward a longer commit; we'll model 30/60/90 day options in the spreadsheet.
[05:31] Sofia: for the pilot we want a 2-week dedicated pool, but small, and then a 30 day ramp if it looks good. how quickly can you provision GPUs in us-west?
[05:43] Eric: provisioning for dedicated pools is usually under 48 hours in us-west for our standard SKUs, 72 hours for specialized quantized runtime. but for pilot we can pre-reserve a small pool so you have near-immediate start.
[06:05] Caleb: who is responsible for the benchmark harness? we have internal load generator but prefer Redwood to run initial 48h burst to compare.
[06:12] Maya: Redwood SE team will run the harness in partnership — we ask you to provide seq len distribution and sample prompts. Eric: i'll own the run and post the results in the shared spreadsheet.
[06:28] Eric: note on metrics — we measure p50/p95/p99, TTFB, cost per 1k tokens, and KV cache hit ratio. we'll also capture cold start percent.
[06:40] Sofia: our target p95 is 120ms for the chat service — can you hit that on the 7B quantized?
[06:47] Eric: depends on seq len; for short seq (<128 tokens) 7B quant can reach sub-100ms p95 on dedicated 1xA100 equivalent. for longer seqs it increases. we'll validate in the benchmark.
[06:58] Liam: what about error budgets and alerting? need SLOs in grafana for us.
[07:04] Maya: we'll provide dashboards and tracing hooks; you can forward traces into your existing observability or use our console for quick view.
[07:15] Unknown Caller: (laugh)
[07:20] Priya: also need a clear show-back for cost to product teams. a per-route breakdown would be ideal.
[07:28] Janelle: the console supports token-level cost and per-route dashboards; we'll include sample screenshots.
[07:36] Sofia: governance — we need guardrails: rate limits per key, content filtering for PII, and role-based access. can those be enforced per route?
[07:46] Eric: yes, RBAC, per-route quotas, and content filters can be applied. for PII we recommend presubmit masks and using private deployments so sensitive prompts never leave the VPC.
[07:59] Caleb: the product ask — we'd like to schedule a canary rollout for feature flags and A/B test across model variants. is that supported?
[08:07] Eric: yes, rollouts and percent traffic splits are first-class; you can do canary or A/B and rollback policies on geographies.
[08:18] Maya: ok let's talk numbers quickly — I'll share a spreadsheet but high level: 30-day small dedicated pool estimated at $XXk/day depending on GPU SKU, plus token costs. Priya, what's a comfortable pilot band?
[08:35] Priya: for a pilot we can commit up to $25k but need the forecast to show upside and conversion potential.
[08:42] Maya: great — we'll shape the pilot to fit.
[08:50] Sofia: a few items from the May incident: 1) need clearer throttling so we don't drop requests, 2) better circuit breaker observability, 3) post-incident RCA. we saw some misattributed logs.
[09:05] Eric: we'll share the RCA summary and a remediation plan — also recommend a rate limiting policy and a short-lived token strategy to isolate traffic bursts.
[09:16] Liam: about the logs — can we export raw inference logs to our S3 for long-term retention?
[09:21] Maya: yes you can forward logs; we support S3 and GCS exports and can help with lifecycle policies.
[09:29] Caleb: do you have examples of customers with similar scale that moved to dedicated and saw cost per request go down?
[09:36] Maya: yes, we have a case study we'll send — anonymized numbers but shows 20-30% cost reduction after tuning batching and quant profiles.
[09:45] Sofia: great. also security question — do you support our KMS vendor (Thalos KMS)?
[09:51] Eric: we integrate with a list of KMS providers; if Thalos isn't on the list we'll engage eng to validate. please add vendor details.
[10:00] Maya: key deliverables: we'll send security pack, a tailored pricing spreadsheet, and pilot proposal by Friday. Eric will draft the benchmark config and run it once you confirm prompts.
[10:12] Priya: timeline sounds good. afterwards we'll reconvene for a budget approval meeting.
[10:20] Janelle: i'll create the pilot kickoff invite and include runbooks.
[10:27] Maya: any final questions?
[10:31] Sofia: nil from me. thanks.
[10:35] Liam: good.
[10:38] Maya: ok thanks everyone. recap and next steps in the calendar invite, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[10:45] (meeting ends, 56:00 elapsed)
